FINDINGS: Respiratory motion artifacts reduced the diagnostic value of the examination. The trachea and both main bronchi were of normal width. No filling defect consistent with PTE was detected in either main pulmonary artery or its visible proximal branches. Heart dimensions were increased. An effusion measuring 10 mm at its thickest point was observed in the pericardial area. No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes were detected in the mediastinum or both hilum. A mosaic attenuation pattern is observed in both lungs. There is a suspicious appearance for a peripherally located ground-glass opacity in the posterior upper lobe of the right lung. However, a clear distinction cannot be made in terms of mosaic attenuation patterns. Clinical evaluation is recommended. Increased interlobular septal thickness is present in both lungs. Left lung ventilation is reduced. A smear-like effusion, measuring approximately 3 mm at its thickest point, was observed in the right hemithorax. Increased thickness of extrapleural fat tissue is observed in both hemithoraxes.

Pleural effusion, reaching a depth of 2 cm at the level of the right lung, and areas of passive atelectasis adjacent to the effusion were observed in both lungs, with the effusion extending into the fissures. Pleural thickening was also present in both lungs. The findings in the lung parenchyma are largely similar to those in the previous CT scan.
